title: 1872 — the year the world closed into a circuit
learning_goal: Know why 1872 was the first year the journey was possible: a port, twelve termini, an underground, an electric street, and a wire that closed round the planet six weeks earlier.

narration.script: Why was 1872 the first year anyone could seriously try this? Because of this: the largest port in the world. Eight hundred thousand tons of cargo a year in 1800; eight million by 1880. Every steamer timetable in the story radiates from here. This film is thirty-one years too late. There is no moving picture of 1872 — this is the Strand in 1903, and it is the closest thing that exists. Close to four million people. A quarter more than Beijing. The river wall he crosses was two years old. In 1878 it became the first street in Britain permanently lit by electricity. Twelve main-line termini by 1865. No other city on earth had anything like that many. The world's first underground railway was nine years old, and carried nine and a half million people in its first year. Between 1870 and 1872 they ran a wire up the middle of Australia — thirty-six thousand poles — to meet the cable from Java. It was finished on the twenty-second of August 1872. From London that October you could telegraph almost anywhere a steamer called. He races the ships. The news about him travels instantly.
